Portfolio / Field report Jakarta, Indonesia · November 2026

Systems for real-world data.

Statistics, data infrastructure, and product design meet in my work. I’m Fikri Septrian Anggara — a system architect and full-stack developer at Statistics Indonesia. I build data platforms, quantitative tools, and design systems for work where the numbers have to hold up.

This edition collects four systems built end to end, and sixteen smaller projects in the archive. Each plate is a working interface, not a mockup.

Plate01

Quantitative systems

alphaIdx — IDX Quant Terminal

An institutional research terminal for the Indonesia Stock Exchange.

Field
Fintech · AI · Data visualisation
Status
Private build
Stack
Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind v4, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Prisma, Gemini, Docker
Link
No public link

A four-pillar screening and research platform for IDX equities: fundamental, bandarmology, technical, and sentiment. It combines quantitative scoring, foreign–domestic broker flow, lot-aware portfolio construction, an AI research assistant, and multi-channel alerts in one terminal.

  1. 01Four screening engines with Top, Mid, and Low tiers, plus dedicated screener pages and CSV export.
  2. 02Capital-aware portfolio builder from Rp 1 million to Rp 10 billion, with IDX lot rounding and mandate profiles.
  3. 03RBAC on PostgreSQL, Gemini-powered quant insight, PDF dossiers, Telegram and WhatsApp alerts, and a PWA shell.

Plate02

Data platforms

KG Smart Search

Natural-language statistics search that lands on verified SQL, not guesses.

Field
Data engineering · Knowledge graph · NLP
Status
Internal build
Stack
Python, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Neo4j, Redis, sqlglot, MapLibre, Apache ECharts
Link
No public link

A neuro-symbolic search layer over BPS statistics. A three-layer knowledge graph bridges Indonesian questions to verified SQL, a natural-language parser extracts entities, and a promptable LLM synthesises a narrative answer with citations. The analyst workspace includes maps, ECharts, dynamic tables, saved queries, and a dashboard builder.

  1. 01Pipeline from natural-language question to entity resolution, SQL, and a cited narrative.
  2. 02Analyst workspace with maps, ECharts, dynamic tables, saved queries, and a dashboard builder.
  3. 03270 green tests and 88/88 deterministic evaluations as recorded in the repository.

Plate03

AI infrastructure

ModelRouter

Routes each prompt to the right model in under 30 ms, by reading its complexity.

Field
AI infrastructure · Developer tools
Status
Open source
Stack
Hono, TanStack Router, React, Vite, TypeScript, Zod, Liquid d1, Ollama, SSE
Link
Repository ↗

A reverse proxy that scores prompt complexity with Liquid d1, then selects a model from a capability, tag, and cost-aware registry. It exposes both OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible endpoints, including bidirectional SSE streaming.

  1. 01Continuous complexity score from 1.00 to 5.00 in a single forward pass.
  2. 02Dual protocol surface: /v1/chat/completions and /v1/messages with streaming.
  3. 03A 16-model registry with routing policies, cost accounting, and deterministic fallback.

Design System Studio

A visual studio that compiles design systems into code, schemas, and AI prompts.

A canvas editor for assembling primitives, tokens, and components, then compiling them into HTML/CSS/JS, JSON Schema, and AI-promptable Markdown. Tokens follow the DTCG format, and component previews stay isolated inside Shadow DOM.

  1. 01Canvas editor with an inspector for layout, typography, tokens, and inheritance.
  2. 02Multi-target compiler: CSS/HTML, JSON Schema, and Markdown written for AI consumption.
  3. 03Theme studio, presets, and an IndexedDB-backed local project store.

III

Notes

The interface is the last mile. The data model is the work.

A short note on method, the kind of work I take on, and the boundary between the system and its surface.

I work at the point where statistics, data infrastructure, and product design meet. At Statistics Indonesia, that means internal tools that make survey data easier to check, publish, and question.1 Outside it, it means terminals, search systems, and developer tools built to be used rather than demoed.

I care about clear boundaries: what a system owns, what it delegates, and how it fails. Before writing a feature I want the data flow, the failure modes, and the trade-off on the table.2 Then I build the smallest version that survives contact with real data.

01System architecture
Domain models, boundaries, and trade-offs before code. I map the data flow first, then choose the smallest system that holds.
02Data engineering
PostgreSQL, pipelines, and knowledge graphs. Correct aggregation and SQL guardrails matter more than a chat interface in front of them.
03Product engineering
End-to-end delivery with Next.js, React, and FastAPI: interface, API, persistence, and the deployment path in one piece.
04Statistical work
Survey data and official BPS figures. Analysis, forecasting, and tools that keep the definitions of the source data intact.
